Booking Holdings — peer benchmark

BKNG-peer-benchmark-2026-10-06 · USD · series 2026-10-07T16:15:00Z · built 2026-10-08 11:25 UTC

The short version

Travelers pay Booking when they book a stay or other travel through its brands. Expedia, Airbnb, and Trip.com take the same kind of booking — hotel, home, or package — with different inventory and geography weight. Expedia is the closest large online travel agency peer on stays and packages. Airbnb is the homes and direct-to-guest alternative. Trip.com is the major international online travel agency with Asia weight, reporting in CNY on Form 20-F.

Booking has the largest USD revenue in the set. Trip.com stays blank on the dollar charts and has its own CNY panel.

Operating income is the honest profit line. Margin is that line divided by revenue. Trip.com’s CNY margin sits on the percent chart because the ratio is currency-neutral. Growth is left blank wherever the year before was a loss or the sign flipped.

Growth is in each company’s own currency; Trip.com is CNY per ADS on its post-2021 share basis. House rule: YoY is blank when the prior year is ≤ 0 or the sign flips. Growth rates are our arithmetic on filed EPS. Booking’s share counts before 2026 are multiplied by 25 for the 2026 split. Trip.com’s FY2019–20 share counts are read from its restated 20-F for now.

Open gaps

  • Printed in the filings but held back pending a data-extraction fix — blank, no stand-in value: Trip.com FY2021Q3 diluted shares (our data repeats the FY2021Q2 count for it).
  • Trip.com quarterly diluted EPS growth is blank on every quarter — our data has its quarterly share counts but not its quarterly EPS.
  • Trip.com quarterly diluted shares before FY2021, including the FY2018–FY2020 fourth quarters, aren’t in our data. They sit before the quarterly chart axis.
  • Trip.com has no USD revenue or operating income — blank on those charts; it has its own CNY panel.
  • Trip.com weekly trailing PE is blank — it reports in CNY, so there is no USD trailing PE.
  • Weekly trailing PE has blank runs. Booking 2020-W31–2025-W13 (244 weeks): its trailing earnings are printed in the filings but held back pending a data-extraction fix. Expedia 2020-W31–2022-W12: its trailing earnings were negative, so there is no PE. Airbnb 2020-W31–2022-W12: it listed in December 2020, and its trailing earnings stayed negative through 2021, so there is no PE.
  • Trip.com diluted EPS for FY2008–FY2012 is blank: those filings count an ADS as a quarter of a share, so the years can’t be put on today’s basis. They sit before the chart axis.
  • Airbnb listed in December 2020: no Airbnb years before FY2020 or quarters before FY2021 in our data, so no Airbnb diluted EPS growth before FY2021 and no revenue or operating-income growth for FY2020 or the FY2021 quarters.
  • Booking FY2015 annual diluted shares are blank (Booking’s share series starts in FY2016).
  • Year-over-year growth on the revenue, operating-income and Trip.com panels is blank where the prior period was a loss or the sign flipped, named in each chart caption: operating income for Booking FY2020–21, Expedia FY2020–21 and Airbnb FY2021 (annual); Booking FY2021Q1–Q2, FY2021Q4 and FY2022Q1–Q2, Expedia FY2021Q1–Q4, FY2022Q1–Q2 and the first quarters of FY2023–FY2026, and Airbnb FY2022Q1–Q2, FY2023Q1, FY2023Q4, FY2024Q1 and FY2024Q4 (quarterly); Trip.com FY2015–17 and FY2020–22.
  • Expedia FY2021Q4 operating income is the full year less the first three quarters, as calculated in our data; its FY2022Q4 operating-income growth is blank because that calculated quarter is its base.
  • Booking FY2015 revenue and operating-income growth is blank: our data starts at FY2015.
  • Forward PE is empty for every name.
  • Geography, inventory mix, room nights, GBV, and take rate aren’t on this page — the peers don’t print the same measure.
